rationale: C06 is a highly plausible drafting source. It is an earlier presidential letter responding to support for the same March 30 foreign-economic-policy message, and it supplies the child with the same core structure: acknowledge the correspondent's support, reaffirm the program, explain why major trade legislation must await fuller consideration, identify interim accomplishments, and connect expanded trade and investment with American prosperity and a stronger free world. C17 and C02 share the policy rationale and administrative background, respectively, but neither matches the child's immediate epistolary purpose and language as closely.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I welcome your support and the support of the many who like you believe that the proposals of my Message of last March are still in the best interest of our people.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It is gratifying to have your letter of May fourteenth expressing strong support for the foreign economic policy proposals contained in my Message to the Congress of March thirtieth.
shared_material.explanation: Both letters open or close by acknowledging a private correspondent's support for the same March 30 proposals.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Time was not available to consider them adequately. I want to emphasize, however, that my Message of March 30, 1954 to the Congress on this subject remains firmly the Administration position. It is my present intention to give high priority to progress in this whole field in planning for next year's legislative program.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Accomplishing enactment of the heart of the program... would, I believe, best be served by careful and deliberate action taken on the basis of extensive and unhurried hearings... the prospect for consideration by the Congress early next year is excellent.
shared_material.explanation: The child compresses C06's explanation that the principal legislation requires deliberate consideration and should receive priority in the next congressional session.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The prudent widening and deepening of the channels of trade and investment by us will not only produce good results in themselves but will encourage similar action by our friends abroad.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This overall program will provide the forward motion in our country essential to progress the world over in raising levels of profitable trade and investment. It is my deep conviction that in this direction lies the greater security for America that comes from a stronger free world.
shared_material.explanation: Both use expanded trade and investment as the mechanism linking American interests to the economic strength and security of the free world.
